learning_outcomes.text: Reinforce knowledge acquired in previous courses.
Solve kinematic problems with relative translational motion.
Apply Newton's laws to describe the causes of motion.
When appropriate, apply energetic considerations to kinetic problems.
Apply Newton's and conservation laws to systems of more than one particle.
Describe planar motion and its causes in real solids.
Solve problems involving heat exchange between bodies.
Introduce the student to solving thermodynamic cycles and heat engines.

assessment_methods.method: Theory and problems grade (final written exam)
Practical grade (practical exam at the end of labs)

assessment_rules: The final exam is mandatory. Other activities are optional. If only the final exam is taken, it accounts for 100% of the grade. If one, two, or three optional activities are completed (each worth 10%), the final exam's weight will be 90%, 80%, or 70% respectively. Approved optional activities are saved for subsequent calls up to December.
